design_upstream: Augrant causal magic and skill progression

player.name: Unnamed Wayfarer
player.location: Dunmarrow, lower well chamber beneath the old bell tower

Ledger Shard.effect: pulls subtly toward genuine magical claims, keyed links, prepared transfers, or bound relationships
limitations: does not reveal whether the connection is hostile
does not identify who created it
does not reveal what lies at the other end automatically

known_techniques.name: Waymark
known_techniques.summary: Prepare a small anchor on a valid surface. Slow, visible, and physically vulnerable.

known_techniques.name: Vector Knot
known_techniques.summary: Redirect a small amount of existing momentum between a moving source and a compatible receiver. Strongest against committed motion.

known_techniques.name: Resonance Sense
known_techniques.summary: Slow observation can detect nearby prepared marks, active transfer effects, or strong residual magical disturbance; it is not omniscient.

limits: Poor geometry or an incompatible receiver can make a transfer fail.
Using magic under pressure requires concentration and can be interrupted.

scene.weather: cold rain after three wet days
canonical_facts: Dunmarrow's gate closes in roughly forty minutes.
Four bodies hang from the execution tree outside town.
One body moved.
Two gate guards have seen the player approaching but appear not to have noticed the movement.
Fresh muddy footprints lead from Dunmarrow to the tree and do not return.
A small geometric transfer symbol is cut into the bark beneath the fourth body.
The Black Tithe remains a working central mystery, not a predetermined single explanation.
The player used Resonance Sense on the hidden disturbance in the drainage ditch.
The sensed effect appears to be actively redirecting motion through the ditch water rather than simply moving the water directly.
The tree carving and the ditch disturbance appear to participate in the same transfer geometry, but the exact relationship is not yet understood.
The player directly asked the concealed ditch entity whether it was their enemy.
The player shouted to alert the Dunmarrow gate guards while keeping the concealed ditch entity in view.
The concealed entity had previously said it was not the player's enemy unless made into one and demanded that the hanging man be cut down.
The player rushed to the execution tree and cut through the active transfer carving with the long knife.
A strong technical read let the player sever the geometry cleanly rather than merely damaging the bark.
The transfer structure collapsed immediately.
The abnormal motion in the ditch ceased.
The hanging man's movements stopped feeding the ditch effect.
The concealed entity lost part of whatever effect had hidden or sustained it.
The player chose to help the hanging man rather than pursue the fleeing entity.
The player cut the hanging man down without causing a serious fall.
The hanging man was alive but weak, with obvious neck compression and breathing difficulty.
The player immediately explained the active transfer mark, the hidden ditch figure, and the abnormal water movement to the approaching guard.
The concealed figure escaped farther along the drainage ditch while attention shifted to the victim.
The player chose not to pursue the escaped entity or investigate the missing boot.
The player left Edrin Vale and the execution-site evidence in the guards' custody.
Dunmarrow closes its town gates at dusk, but there is no established general stay-indoors curfew.
The player chose to meet Dunmarrow's reeve immediately after entering town.
The meeting takes place in the gatehouse while Edrin Vale is being treated nearby.

The player gave Reeve Maelin Voss a complete truthful account of the execution-ground incident, including speaking to the concealed entity, using Resonance Sense, the entity's demand to cut Edrin down, the transfer link, alerting the guards, severing the mark, seeing the fleeing figure, and Edrin's missing boot.
The player reconstructed the execution-tree transfer mark from memory for Reeve Maelin Voss.
The reconstruction preserved the two-receiver structure and the severed hooked diagonal closely enough to support further analysis.
After the dormant bell tower rang and Resonance Sense reacted, the player asked Reeve Maelin Voss whether she wanted to investigate it.
The player urged the group to hurry to the old bell tower.
The player, Reeve Maelin Voss, and two watchmen reached the tower without stopping to investigate anything else en route.
The player ordered the group to stay together: investigate below the bell tower first, then go upstairs.
The player explicitly checked whether anyone in the group had a shield before committing.
The player attempted to sever the active transfer path beneath the bell tower using the same principle as at the execution tree.
The older network contained redundant/overflow routing. The cut did not stop the system; it caused a violent local discharge through the player's knife and arm.
The player took 4 damage, dropped the knife, and suffered temporary numbness/shock in the weapon hand.
The discharge fed additional motion into the bell above, causing it to ring again.
The failure revealed that this network reroutes interrupted transfer rather than simply collapsing when one path is cut.
After the failed cut, the player recovered the knife with the left hand and paused to observe the underground bell-tower transfer network before going upstairs.
A strong observation showed the basin objects act as person-specific anchors, while the iron rods carry transferred mechanical energy upward.
The network has redundant channels, but the rerouting is not instantaneous: there are brief moments where pressure shifts between paths.
The bell above is acting as a major receiver/reservoir and is currently closer to another discharge than before.
The player identified that blindly cutting more channels is likely to worsen the situation.
The player ordered a shield-and-reach formation on the spiral stair.
Harl holds the choke point with shield raised while Joren uses the spear from behind him; the player remains behind them due to the impaired right hand.
During the stairwell fight, the player used Vector Knot against the robed man's committed downhill lunge.
The player redirected a small portion of the attacker's existing momentum sideways and downward into the inner stair geometry rather than trying to stop him outright.
The attacker lost his footing, struck the stone steps/inner wall, and collapsed immediately in front of Harl's shield.
The shield-and-spear formation prevented the falling attacker from crashing through into the player.
The player attacked the prone robed man with the long knife using the left hand while the right remained impaired.
The attack landed cleanly and caused a serious but not immediately fatal wound.
The player ordered the group to hold formation and stop attacking the bell-linked man.
The player explicitly recognized two constraints: blindly damaging the underground network is dangerous, and injuring the linked man feeds the bell.
The player used Resonance Sense at point-blank range on the bell-linked man's throat markings while the party held formation and stopped attacking.
The throat markings are not themselves the full transfer circuit; they are a keyed coupling layer that ties the man's pulse and involuntary movement to the tower network.
The connection has a narrow synchronization point just below the left side of the jaw where three carved lines converge.
The bell is receiving the man's movement and physiological shock as transferable mechanical input.
The connection can likely be interrupted by breaking synchronization rather than by cutting flesh or destroying the main network.
A brief disruption of rhythm, pressure, or alignment at the convergence point may be enough to desynchronize the coupling.
Because the link is keyed to the man, a prepared Waymark could potentially be used as a temporary false receiver if the timing is precise.
The player prepared a Waymark on the inner stair wall as a false receiver for the bell-linked man's keyed transfer.
The player tuned the Waymark to imitate the man's coupling signature closely enough for the network to recognize it during a reroute window.
At the moment the network shifted paths, the player used Vector Knot to redirect the live transfer into the prepared Waymark.
The false receiver accepted the transfer long enough to desynchronize the man from the bell without further injuring him.
The Waymark overloaded and fractured after the transfer, but the discharge went into the stone wall rather than into a person.
The bell's motion dropped sharply once the living link was broken.
One bronze waymark nail was consumed/damaged in the overloaded false receiver.
The player attempted to recover Resonance by attuning a fresh Wayfarer working to the bell network rather than siphoning stored mechanical energy directly.
The attunement failed: the ancient network did not accept the player's pattern as a stable participant.
No Resonance was recovered and no additional damage was taken.
The failed attunement produced a return pulse that made it clear the newly opened structure below is now the strongest active node in the local transfer network.
The party returned downstairs without splitting.
The newly opened mechanism revealed a lower passage beneath the original basement chamber.
The player remained at 6/10 HP, 0/3 Resonance, with the right hand still impaired.
At the lower well chamber, the player refused to return anything blindly and demanded that the unseen speaker identify itself first.
The player asked the entity known as Keeper Below to explain its role.
The player challenged the Keeper Below to provide evidence that its explanation was truthful.
The player accepted the Keeper Below's reversible test.
The party stayed together, retrieved Edrin Vale's missing boot from the basin above, and returned to the lower well chamber.
The player kept physical possession of the boot and did not place it into the socket or surrender it.
When the boot was brought close to Edrin Vale's carved name, the name and empty socket reacted immediately.
The boot pulled slightly toward the socket as if under tension, while the chain below slackened a fraction.
The bell above did not ring.
The reaction occurred before the boot touched the socket, supporting the Keeper's claim that the personal object functions as a keyed token tied to Edrin's claim.
The player inserted Edrin Vale's missing boot into the keyed socket beside his name while the party held formation.
The socket accepted the token without violent discharge.
Edrin Vale's carved name faded from active resonance and the chain below slackened significantly.
The bell remained still.
The boot lost its keyed resonance and became an ordinary damaged personal object after the claim released.
The result strongly supports the Keeper Below's claim that placing the keyed token releases the stored claim associated with that person.
After releasing Edrin Vale's claim, the player asked the Keeper Below for a physical item in exchange for continued help.
The player accepted the Keeper Below's Ledger Shard reward.
The Ledger Shard is now in the player's possession.
The shard gives a slight physical pull when brought near an object participating in a genuine magical claim, keyed link, prepared transfer, or bound relationship.
The shard does not identify purpose, danger, creator, or target; it only confirms that a real connection exists.
GM correction: the player has not agreed to release additional claims, revive anyone, or work for the Keeper Below. Any such future involvement requires an explicit player choice.
The player ended involvement in the bell-tower investigation for the night and told Reeve Maelin Voss to come find them if further help was needed.
Reeve Maelin Voss accepted the boundary and did not pressure the player to continue immediately.
No new plot event was introduced solely to prevent the player from leaving.
The player paid 2 silver for supper and a bed at a travelers' inn.
A safe full night's rest restored 4 HP under the locked recovery formula: floor(25% of 10 max HP) + CON modifier 2.
The player's temporary right-hand shock/numbness cleared because it had not been recorded as a true Wound.
Resonance remained at 0/3 because sleep does not automatically restore Resonance.
No one came to fetch the player during the night.
The player returned to the old bell tower the next morning specifically to visit the Keeper Below.
The player was allowed back into the secured tower because of their direct involvement in the previous night's investigation.
The player descended to the lower well chamber without restarting the broader investigation.
The player told the Keeper Below: 'You are very powerful.'
The Keeper Below described its power as narrow, old, and domain-bound rather than general omnipotence.
The player asked the Keeper Below whether it had once been human.
The Keeper Below answered that it had once been human, but implied that the transformation into its present role was gradual and bound to the system it serves.
The player asked the Keeper Below whether it wanted freedom.
The Keeper Below did not give an immediate simple yes/no answer; it expressed uncertainty about what freedom would mean after so long bound to its role.
The player asked the Keeper Below who the most powerful human it had ever met was.
The Keeper named Sereth Vale, a human transfer-worker remembered for extreme precision and control rather than spectacle.

According to the Keeper, Sereth could redirect structural loads, momentum, heat, and pressure across prepared systems without collapsing them, and once stabilized a failing stone bridge long enough for hundreds to cross.
The Keeper described Sereth as powerful because she understood limits well enough to act at the edge of them without losing control.
The player asked the Keeper Below to teach them.
The Keeper Below agreed in principle to teach within its domains: claims, bindings, keyed transfers, anchors, conservation, and precise transfer structure.
The Keeper made clear that instruction would not instantly grant mastery; learning would require demonstration, practice, correction, and risk-appropriate exercises.
During the first formal lesson, the player defined transfer as 'magic from one point to another.'

The Keeper corrected the definition: transfer magic does not simply move 'magic'; it establishes a lawful relationship in which a specific quantity, state, or claim moves or is reassigned from a source to a receiver under defined constraints.
The Keeper emphasized that source, transferable quantity, receiver, compatibility, capacity, and consequence must all be identified.

learning.reason: Received direct instruction distinguishing generic magical movement from source-quantity-receiver transfer structure.

last_correction.issue: The GM previously used the word 'curfew' too broadly.
last_correction.correction: Only gate closure is canonical; ordinary movement inside town after gate closure is allowed unless a later event establishes otherwise.
